name: Standard Route (South Ridge / South Gully via Copper Glance Basin)

waypoints.name: Copper Glance Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Winthrop, drive north about 8 miles on West Chewuch Road (County Road 1213) to Eightmile Road (Forest Road 5130). Follow Eightmile Road roughly 12 to 15 miles northwest along Eightmile Creek to the Copper Glance Trailhead, at about 3,800 feet. There is no fee here.

waypoints.name: Copper Glance Creek crossing
waypoints.directions: Follow Copper Glance Trail #519 up the old mining road about 1.5 miles to the ruins of the Copper Glance mine, cross Copper Glance Creek (a ford when the bridge is out, high in early season), and continue through burned forest past a small pond to Copper Glance Lake at about 6,260 ft. Carry on into the open basin above the lake to the creek crossing at about 6,400 ft; fill water here, as there is none higher up.

waypoints.name: Copper Glance Basin camp
waypoints.directions: From the crossing, walk a short way north-west up the basin to the knoll at about 6,600 ft that serves as the usual camp.

waypoints.name: West Craggy Peak summit
waypoints.directions: Walk up into the cirque directly beneath the peak and take the chute that slants up and right across the headwall to a col on the south ridge; it often holds a streak of snow into summer, and the right one heads for a notch in the skyline rather than steepening into a wall. Above the col, class 2 rock and a short upper couloir lead onto the easy summit ridge and the top.

approach_variants.name: Copper Glance Basin and the south-side chute
approach_variants.notes: West Craggy is the lower of the two Craggy summits and is normally climbed on the same trip as its neighbour, the two being joined by a saddle. The approach is short by the standards of this country: a forest road reaches the trailhead and the Copper Glance trail reaches the open basin in a few miles, starting on an old mining jeep track, passing the mine ruins, crossing the creek where the bridge has been out in various years, and running through burn to the lake and the basin above it. A knoll at about 6,600 ft in the basin is the usual camp. The climbing is class 2 with occasional short scrambling, and the two real considerations are loose rock and how much snow is left in the gully.
hazards: Sustained loose talus and scree with real rockfall potential in the gully
Steep residual snow in the chute into early or mid summer
Cornices and avalanche terrain if attempted in winter or spring
High water at the Copper Glance Creek crossing in early season
No water above the basin crossing
Class 3 downclimbing with exposure if the direct descent line is taken
approach_variants.baseFinding: From the camp knoll at about 6,600 ft in Copper Glance Basin, walk up into the cirque that sits directly beneath the peak. The base of the climb is a chute cutting the cirque headwall, slanting up to the right as you face the wall, and it is the feature to find because it is the one line that tops out at a col on the south ridge rather than dead-ending under rock. Snow lies in it well into summer and often that snow is the easiest way to identify it from across the basin, a white streak in an otherwise brown-grey wall. Several other runnels drain the same cirque and they look similar from below; the discriminator is where they finish, so follow one that is heading toward a notch in the skyline ridge rather than one that steepens into a wall. Above the col, class 2 rock and a short upper couloir lead onto an easy summit ridge. There is a second way to reach the same ground: from the saddle at roughly 7,600 ft shared with Big Craggy, traverse just below the crest on its south side to a small notch that opens into a talus-and-rock gully, and take that. Fill water at the creek crossing near 6,400 ft, because there is none above it. If you find yourself under a cliff band with no way through, the useful move is to drop back into the basin and re-enter by a different chute rather than to force a line through class 3 ground with exposure.
